Arrow Electronics (ARW) Launches ArrowSphere Cloud Portal, Is The 16% Undervaluation Case Convincing?

ARW

Arrow Electronics (ARW) drew fresh attention after unveiling a limited release of its ArrowSphere Cloud sales portal, a tool built to help partners manage Microsoft and AWS cloud opportunities using AI driven sales intelligence.

Recent trading has cooled some of Arrow Electronics' earlier momentum, with the share price down 13.15% over the past 30 days and 9.33% over 90 days. This comes even after a year to date share price return of 64.88% and a 1 year total shareholder return of 77.00% that point to strong longer term gains, as investors weigh the new cloud portal launch alongside November's earnings beat, fresh guidance, buyback activity and leadership changes.

Spot fresh AI and cloud momentum plays alongside Arrow Electronics by scanning our handpicked 53 AI infrastructure stocks.

Bulls see Arrow Electronics as a cloud and AI execution story that the recent pullback has simply put on sale. Bears argue the rally already prices in the earnings beat, new tools and buybacks. Which case does the current valuation support?

Most Popular Narrative: 16% Undervalued

Arrow Electronics closed at $186.38, while the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St places fair value at $222.50 using a 9.61% discount rate. That gap frames a story that leans on AI, cloud demand and higher margin services to support the thesis.

Accelerating adoption of cloud, infrastructure software, cybersecurity and AI related workloads, reflected in ECS billings of more than US$6.4b in Q1 2026 and a backlog that was over 75% higher year over year by Q2 2026, increases Arrow Electronics exposure to higher margin software and services that can influence revenue mix and non GAAP margins.

See why 3 investors see Arrow Electronics as 16% undervalued.

Result: Fair Value of $222.50 (UNDERVALUED)

Still, the story around Arrow Electronics can change quickly if ECS restructuring drags on margins or if insider selling and premium valuation worries return to the foreground.

Find out about the key risks to this Arrow Electronics narrative.

Another View: Arrow Electronics On Cash Flow

The story shifts when you switch from analyst fair value to the Simply Wall St DCF model. On that framework, Arrow Electronics at $186.38 trades above an estimated future cash flow value of $113.02, which screens as overvalued rather than cheap. Which lens do you trust more for your own process?

title: Microsoft Stock (MSFT) Forecast – Mizuho Stays Bullish on Strong Revenue Growth Prospects

Microsoft Stock (MSFT) Forecast – Mizuho Stays Bullish on Strong Revenue Growth Prospects

MSFT

ANT
CRM

Tech giant Microsoft (MSFT) unveiled new AI models at its Ignite conference amid intense competition from AI players OpenAI and Anthropic (ANT). Reacting to the updates at the conference, Mizuho analyst Gregg Moskowitz reiterated a Buy rating on MSFT stock with a price target of $625. The analyst believes MSFT's revenue growth prospects over the medium term and beyond are stronger than many expect, and he remains "very bullish on its tangible AI adoption and monetization levers."

Moskowitz ranks No. 426 among more than 12,500 analysts on TipRanks. He has a 62% success rate with an average return per rating of 11.6% over a one-year period.

Mizuho Highlights Key Takeaways from Microsoft's Ignite Conference

Moskowitz highlighted key announcements from the first day of the Ignite conference, including an expanded deal with Salesforce (CRM) that brings Salesforce data into Copilot and enhanced FinOps for AI capabilities in Agent 365 Business Analytics.

Furthermore, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said that he is confident about the company's competitive positioning and strategic direction. In a discussion with investors and analysts, Nadella said that there will be an increasing demand for a multi-model system, including open weights and a decision engine that directs tasks across models.

Additionally, Moskowitz noted that Nadella expects continued strength in Microsoft's competitive position, saying that "hyperscale is about the long tail of workloads and customers rather than being tethered to one or two frontier labs." Looking ahead, Nadella is confident about Copilot pricing, as he believes that Microsoft can offer the best models through usage-based billing while continuing to deliver value via its subscription model.

MSFT stock has risen only 5% so far this year as investors are concerned about returns on the company's massive AI spending.

Is Microsoft Stock a Buy, Hold, or Sell?

Given the long-term growth opportunities, Wall Street has a Strong Buy consensus rating on Microsoft stock based on 35 Buys and four Holds. The average MSFT stock price target of $632.48 indicates about 25% upside potential.

title: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 in historic $1 trillion offering
detail:
Anthropic prices IPO at $83 in historic $1 trillion offering
Madison Mills
Wed, November 18, 2026 at 3:16 PM MST 1 min read
ANT
NVDA
GOOGN
MSFT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Anthropic on Thursday priced its long-awaited IPO at $83 per share, Axios has confirmed, which would give the Claude maker an initial market cap of $1.08 trillion and a fully diluted value of around $1.5 trillion.

Why it matters: Wall Street expects the AI boom to continue, despite some recent tumult.

Zoom in: Anthropic priced much higher than its planned range of $70 to $78 per share.

The company also could raise significantly more money if underwriters exercise their so-called "greenshoe" option, while Anthropic also will receive $26 billion via a concurrent private placement from tech giants like Nvidia, Google and Microsoft.

Axios has not yet been able to confirm the number of shares offered. Anthropic had said it planned to sell 825 million shares, which would work out to a $68.5 billion raise (plus the private placement), but it may increase the share count.

Allocation decisions are expected to last several hours on Thursday evening.

For context: Anthropic was valued at $965 billion in its most recent private round. The apples-to-apples comparison would be with the fully diluted value.

SpaceX raised $75 billion in its IPO and a total of $86.25 billion with the exercised greenshoe, at a higher valuation than Anthropic.

What we're watching: Shares are expected to begin trading Thursday, Nov. 19, on the Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT."
